text:
Jordan Staal won the Conn Smythe Trophy last spring as Carolina won the Stanley Cup, and this season has been hard on him. He's 38, he missed most of October and early November, and he has no goals and two points in ten games. The Hockey Writers ran a piece this week saying his struggles should concern the Hurricanes.

The numbers back up the concern on offense and soften it elsewhere. He has 1.5 expected goals and nothing to show for it, and his talent range expects a shooting percentage far north of zero. At five on five Carolina gets 65% of the shot attempts with him on, but the chance quality is ordinary and the team is better without him.

He's back where he belongs, though: two assists in his last two games, including the setup on Eric Robinson's shorthanded goal at Madison Square Garden. That's the job.

Weekend footnote: Sebastian Aho passed his brother Eric for the most goals in franchise history since relocation. What to watch: whether the shutdown work catches up to the Conn Smythe version before the playoffs do.
